guides.definition: Requests JSON over HTTP, raises on an error status, and decodes the response body. Requires requests in the selected Python environment; Hypershell does not install it.

parameters.name: timeout
parameters.description: Connection and read timeout in seconds.

examples.title: Read an API status
examples.code:
import requests

response = requests.get("https://api.example.com/status", timeout=10)
response.raise_for_status()
data = response.json()
examples.explanation: An explicit timeout prevents an unbounded wait; raise_for_status keeps HTTP failures out of the success path.

guides.definition: Serializes a Python value as JSON and validates the response status. Requires requests in the selected Python environment; Hypershell does not install it.

parameters.name: timeout
parameters.description: Connection and read timeout in seconds.

examples.title: Create a job
examples.code:
import requests

payload = {"name": "Atlas", "enabled": True}
response = requests.post("https://api.example.com/jobs", json=payload, timeout=10)
response.raise_for_status()
examples.explanation: The json argument handles JSON encoding and the content type; validate any API-specific response contract after the status check.

guides.definition: Creates a Requests session with shared headers and uses it for a request. Requires requests in the selected Python environment; Hypershell does not install it.

parameters.name: headers
parameters.description: Dictionary of headers shared by session requests.

parameters.name: timeout
parameters.description: Connection and read timeout in seconds.

examples.title: Reuse an API accept header
examples.code:
import requests

with requests.Session() as session:
    session.headers.update({"Accept": "application/json"})
    response = session.get("https://api.example.com/status", timeout=10)
    response.raise_for_status()
examples.explanation: A session reuses connection pools and shared configuration; the context manager closes its resources deterministically.
